purpose: Oteseconazole is used to reduce the chance of getting repeat vaginal yeast infections in women who are not able to get pregnant. It is specifically for women who keep getting these infections over and over again (three or more times a year). It is NOT used to treat an active yeast infection that you have right now.
how_it_works: Oteseconazole works by blocking a specific enzyme that the yeast fungus needs to build its outer protective layer called the cell membrane. Without this protective layer, the fungus cannot survive and grow. Because it targets something very specific to the fungus, it is designed to work well without interfering as much with your body's natural processes.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, and changes in your menstrual period such as irregular or painful periods. Some women may also notice diarrhea or stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine must NOT be taken if you are pregnant, trying to get pregnant, or could become pregnant, because it can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. You need to use reliable birth control during treatment and for a period of time after finishing it — your doctor will tell you exactly how long. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medications you take, because oteseconazole can interact with many other drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual dosing starts with a higher loading dose taken by mouth once a day for the first two days, followed by a lower maintenance dose taken once a week. Your doctor will give you a specific schedule to follow. Always take it exactly as prescribed and finish the full course even if you feel fine.
